LESSON: WRITING 4.3.1 WRITING TO GIVE INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Writing 4.3.1 Writing to give information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 4.3.1 Writing to give information, part of Strand 4 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to understand how to respond to an emergency?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch a short video or read a passage on the process of responding to an emergency,

2. work with peers to summarise

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a short video or read a passage on the process of responding to an emergency,
2. work with peers to summarise

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 4.3.1 Writing to give information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: The learner interacts with digital content to watch a short video or read a passage on the process of

responding to an emergency.

• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: This is enhanced as the learner analyses concepts logically to outline the main steps

taken in responding to the emergency in the video or passage.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner exhibits accountability to accept constructive feedback by presenting the composition to other

members of class for peer review.

• Love: This is promoted as the learner displays trustworthiness when organising their best compositions in a portfolio.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security: This is promoted as the learner interacts with information on how to respond to an emergency.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of safety at school to their learning of safety in Pre-Technical Studies.
